newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to privatize its first state bank Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to privatize its first state bank Tuesday.

text.p: After two failed attempts last year, Brazil hopes to finally privatize its first state bank Tuesday, but the sale of Rio de Janeiro's Banerj hinges on Senate approval of a deal resolving the bank's pension-related debts.

The Senate must approve a 2.9 billion real loan from federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal (CEF) allowing Rio state to assume all of Banerj's debts to its pension fund, a key factor in maintaining investor interest.

The loan was approved by Rio de Janeiro state Legislative Assembly Friday, but Congress' Senate must still give it a green light before the auction takes place as planned at 1400 local time/1700 GMT on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange.

Paulo Ferraz, president of private bank Bozano, Simonsen which was hired to manage Banerj, said the sale could be delayed for a few hours or until the following day if the Senate does not approve the loan by the auction's scheduled time.
"Of course there is a probability that the floor of the Senate will not be able to approve the loan before the auction's time. But we will only know that tomorrow," he told Reuters.
Ferraz said he is more concerned by a host of lawsuits against Banerj's privatization auction.
So far, seven lawsuits have been filed against Banerj's sell-off, which could suspend the sale if any of them result in court injunctions at the last minute.
Last year, the state failed twice to sell the bank due to poor investor interest caused by worries over debt and court injunctions.
To facilitate the sell-off, Rio state cut Banerj's base price to 310 million reais from 480 million reais.

It also allowed investors to pay for 100 percent of the bank's auction price with federal and state privatization bonds, which makes the bank even cheaper as those bonds can be purchased at 60-70 percent of their face value.

Four banks -- Bradesco, Banco Itau, BCN and Cia de Investimentos Latino-Americana, owned by a foreign bank and represented by local Banco Pactual -- signed up for the auction Friday when they presented the necessary financial guarantees.
The future owner of Banerj, formally known as Banco Banerj SA, will acquire a bank with total assets of 4.5 billion reais and a net worth of 181 million reais.
Banerj has been under Central Bank control since December 1994, but has been managed by Bozano on behalf of the Central Bank since January 1996 to ready it for privatization.

In private hands, the bank showed improved results. Time deposits rose 6.07 percent to 1.163 billion reais in December last year from 1.096 billion reais in 1995, while savings accounts at the bank increased 20.53 percent to 931.3 million reais from 772.7 million reais in the same period.
Revenues from banking services jumped 122.98 percent to 12.5 million reais from 5.6 million reais.
Banerj's branch network was cut to 193 branches from 220, while its staff was reduced to 7,435 employees from 12,000.
